scope: Preserve three user-approved T-shirt-folding videos, compile them into a non-overrideable positive-reference harness, create a synchronized comparison, and publish the result on the PhiAgent demo.
summary: Three 8-second visual results are retained as distinct alternating, staged, and synchronized proposal references. A dependency-light compiler binds each reference to its compatible strategy plan while preserving every hard gate and human veto. The synchronized showcase and website integration are complete, but the evidence remains visual rather than physical execution.

lessons: Matched camera, scene, embodiment, duration, frame rate, and terminal dwell make choreography differences legible.
Positive visual examples should guide approach, contact cadence, arm-role separation, and terminal readability without supplying automatic gate outcomes.
Candidate allocation should branch on sleeve order before sampling so best-of-N does not collapse onto one attractive choreography.
The original full-resolution videos must remain beside a scaled comparison because presentation media is not evaluation evidence.
limitations: User approval covers visual generation quality, not every automatic physical gate.
The first frames are scene-matched but not pixel-identical; SSIM against the alternating reference is 0.936417 and 0.939120 for the other two videos.
No calibrated cloth geometry, force, tactile data, exact joint trajectory, collision-safety result, or real-robot execution evidence is available.
next_actions: Use the bank only for bounded strategy-compatible proposal generation and rerun all frozen automatic gates on every new candidate.
Require candidate-SHA-bound native-resolution review before promoting any future physically evaluated generation.
